test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-II Official Paper-I (Held On: 20 Jan, 2025)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

A lot of people are still ______ over the GDP issue.
solution: The correct answer is: **Option 2**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The word **"sitting on the fence"** means to be undecided or not to take sides in a dispute. (निर्णय न कर पाना या किसी पक्ष में न जाना) • **Example:** Many voters are still sitting on the fence, unable to decide who to vote for. • **"over the fence"** refers to something that is beyond a boundary or limit, but it is not an idiom used for indecision. (सीमा के पार) • **Example:** The ball went over the fence into the neighbor's yard. • **"by the fence"** means near the fence, and is not an idiom related to indecision. (बाड़ के पास) • **Example:** She stood by the fence watching the sunset. • **"breaking a leg"** is an idiom used to wish someone good luck, especially before a performance. (शुभकामनाएँ देना) • **Example:** Break a leg! I know you'll do great in your play tonight. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 1: over the fence** (सीमा के पार): This phrase refers to something beyond a boundary, but it does not relate to indecision. • **Example:** The ball went over the fence into the neighbor's yard. • **Option 3: by the fence** (बाड़ के पास): This phrase means near the fence, and is not related to indecision. • **Example:** She stood by the fence watching the sunset. • **Option 4: breaking a leg** (शुभकामनाएँ देना): This idiom is used to wish someone good luck, typically before a performance. • **Example:** Break a leg! I know you'll do great in your play tonight. a5:Tbf4, The correct answer is 'finest'.
